newsitem.title: USA: Salomon ups Mexico, cuts Chile in LatAm portfolio.
newsitem.headline: Salomon ups Mexico, cuts Chile in LatAm portfolio.

text.p: Salomon Brothers analyst John Mullin raised Mexico's weighting and cut Chile's Tuesday in his model Latin American stocks portfolio.
"We are increasing our overweight recommendation for the Mexican market and decreasing our (already underweight) position in Chile," he wrote in a report.
He raised Mexico's position to 25 percent from 23 percent in the portfolio. Neutral is 22 percent.
Chile was cut to 9.8 percent from 11.8 percent. Its neutral weighting is 13.2 percent.

Mullin said in part his opinion of Mexico had been boosted by Sunday's landmark elections. Mexico's long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party lost control of Congress and a leftist opponent won the mayor's office of Mexico City.
"In our view, Mexico is the most attractive value play of the large Latin American markets," he wrote.

"... In Chile positive macroeconomic developments have put wind in the sails of the equity market so far this year. ... In our view, much of the good news is already incorporated in market valuations, which are quite high by regional standards."
